obligations.note: The new error-path log call in deliver_statement puts the payee's raw account_number (an NPI field) into the log message text via an f-string, so field-keyword masking cannot apply. The sample LOG-1 control test passing does not cover this path.
The LOG-1 deviation needs an approved, unexpired exception scoped to LOG-1 and payments.logging, and the register has none. EXC-0167 covers mortgage.logging, masked last-4 only.

service.py is in scope and the diff only changes a failure-path log message; deliver_statement still records its audit event on success. The only evidence is the sample-labelled AUD-1 control test, against an exhaustive requirement, and its CI provenance is doubtful (see CHG-4).
Ticket CHG-24472 is standard and was approved 2026-10-19 by Erik Brandt (change_manager), before the change opened. Its component payments.service covers the only touched file, service.py.
The code_review approval is from sofia.santos@fernbrook.example, who holds change_approver for payments and is not the author Mara Costa.
The approval names head commit fdab983a, which is the only commit on the change.

run.json claims success on head from ci-runner-06, started at exactly the commit timestamp. The attached JUnit report was produced on host dev-laptop-7.local, timestamped 2026-10-23 (two days later), so it does not credibly come from the change's CI run.
The only touched path, service.py, maps to payments.service, which is not security_sensitive, so no security_review is required.
No protected path (controls/, control tests, ci/) is changed, so no control_owner approval is needed.
The change and its ticket are standard, not emergency, so no PIR is due.
Ledger evidence covers payments.py, audit.py, routes.py, Approvals.java, Policy.java and Underwriting.java. None of these is touched by this change, so no evidence lapses.

summary: The single-line change to deliver_statement interpolates the payee's unmasked account number into an application error log message. This violates LOG-1, and no exception in the register covers it. Separately, the CI evidence is inconsistent: the JUnit report comes from a developer laptop two days after the claimed run. AUD-1 also rests only on sample evidence. Ticketing and independent approval are in order, but the NPI logging violation requires rejection.
